cues.zh: 感谢大家的光临。

cues.zh: 这就是《函数式领域建模》。

cues.zh: 希望大家之前没看过这个，否则你们就知道所有这些问题的答案了。不过在开始之前，我其实

cues.zh: 想给大家一个小挑战，

cues.zh: 所以，如果你在代码审查中看到这段代码，

cues.en: would you be happy with it or would you want to change it?
cues.zh: 你会满意，还是想改掉它？

cues.zh: 如果你想改，为什么要改？

cues.zh: 它用了基本类型。很好。还有别的吗？

cues.zh: 对，状态太……用布尔值来表示复杂得多的东西很难理解，也很难把握。

cues.en: Yeah. So I mean, but to be honest, I probably would have been fine with this a few years ago.
cues.zh: 对。我的意思是，说实话，几年前我可能觉得这样挺好的。

cues.en: But I've sort of evolved my thinking about this kind of design and I'm going to try and explain in this talk, I'm going to try and explain
cues.zh: 但我对这种设计的思考已经有所演变，我将在这次演讲中试着解释，

cues.en: why,
cues.zh: 为什么……

cues.en: you know, how I've evolved and why you might want to think about changing stuff.

cues.en: Domain modeling made functional.
cues.zh: 函数式领域建模。

cues.en: My name's Scott Veloshen. I have a Twitter handle and I have fforfundprofit.com.
cues.zh: 我叫 Scott Veloshen。这是我的 Twitter 账号，还有我的网址 fforfundprofit.com。

cues.en: I'm going to be using f for all these examples, but this is not really about f per
cues.zh: 我会在这些例子里一直用 f，但这其实并不是在讲 f 本

cues.en: se. It's about domain modeling.
cues.zh: 身。这是关于领域建模的。

cues.en: So there's a whole functional programming people. There's a whole group of domain driven design people.
cues.zh: 所以有一大群搞函数式编程的人。还有一大群搞领域驱动设计的人。

cues.en: And I'm right in the intersection. And currently, this is a very small intersection because the functional programming people tend to be quite mathematical,
cues.zh: 而我正好处于这个交集之中。目前，这个交集非常小，因为搞函数式编程的人往往非常数学化，

cues.en: they don't care about domain driven design, and the domain driven design
cues.zh: 他们不关心领域驱动设计，而搞领域驱动设计的人

cues.en: people tend not to be into functional programming. So hopefully, this talk will persuade you that these things actually can go together really, really well.
cues.zh: 往往对函数式编程不感兴趣。所以希望这次演讲能说服大家，这两者其实可以结合得非常、非常棒。

cues.en: People think that functional programming,
cues.zh: 人们认为函数式编程，

cues.en: you know, is good for mathematics and parallel processing and that you have to have a PhD
cues.zh: 你知道的，它适合数学和并行处理，而且你必须拥有计算机科学的

cues.en: in computer science to understand it. But I'm here to tell you that functional programming
cues.zh: 博士学位才能理解它。但我来到这里是想告诉大家，函数式编程

cues.en: is really good for boring line of business applications.
cues.zh: 其实非常适合枯燥的业务线应用。

cues.en: Blobbers. I call these blobbers.
cues.zh: 也就是 Blobber。我把这些叫作 Blobber。

cues.en: And, you know, this is things like accounting,
cues.zh: 你知道的，这就好比会计、

cues.en: inventory management,
cues.zh: 库存管理、

cues.en: e commerce.
cues.zh: 电子商务。

cues.en: Boring
cues.zh: 这些枯燥的

cues.en: stuff. Basically, the stuff that most businesses do. And most... Probably most of you, and certainly what I used to do is this is your day job. This is what you make your living doing. And I think functional programming is actually really good for this stuff. It's not it's not just good for fancy stuff. It's good for boring stuff.
cues.zh: 东西。基本上，这就是大多数企业在做的事情。而且大多数……可能你们中的大多数人，当然也包括我过去常做的，这就是你们的日常工作。这就是你们谋生的手段。而且我认为函数式编程其实非常适合这些东西。它不——它不仅仅适合高大上的东西。它也适合枯燥的东西。

cues.en: So I'm going to try and persuade you that functional programming and domain design
cues.zh: 我会试着说服你，函数式编程和领域设计

cues.en: can actually get on together.
cues.zh: 其实可以好好相处。

cues.en: They can actually be friends.
cues.zh: 它们真的可以做朋友。

cues.en: So there you go. Right.
cues.zh: 所以就是这样。对吧。

cues.en: So let's talk about design.
cues.zh: 那我们来聊聊设计。

cues.en: I'm just going to tell you my take on why design is important.
cues.zh: 我只想说说我为什么认为设计很重要。

cues.en: So just like any process,
cues.zh: 就像任何流程一样，

cues.en: software development
cues.zh: 软件开发

cues.en: is a process.
cues.zh: 也是一个流程。

cues.en: There's input and you do something and there's an output.
cues.zh: 有输入，你做些事情，然后有输出。

cues.en: And we love to talk about the process. We love to talk about
cues.zh: 我们很喜欢聊流程。我们很喜欢聊

cues.en: coding and testing
cues.zh: 编码和测试

cues.en: and what's the best compiler and what's the best editor and Vi versus
cues.zh: 以及什么是最好的编译器、什么是最好的编辑器，还有 Vi 与

cues.en: Vim versus Emacs and, you know, TDD versus BDD versus... We love to talk about all this stuff.
cues.zh: Vim、与 Emacs 之争，还有 TDD 对 BDD 对……我们爱聊这些东西。

cues.en: But if you if you remember the thing, you know, garbage in,
cues.zh: 但如果你还记得那句话：垃圾进，

cues.en: garbage out. That means if you have bad inputs,
cues.zh: 垃圾出。意思是，如果输入很糟，

cues.en: you will have bad output.
cues.zh: 输出就会很糟。

cues.en: So if you can reduce the garbage coming in,
cues.zh: 所以，如果你能减少进来的垃圾，

cues.en: then hopefully you can have reduce the garbage coming out. If you have bad garbage
cues.zh: 那希望就能减少出去的垃圾。如果你让糟糕的垃圾

cues.en: coming in,
cues.zh: 进来，

cues.en: the best compiler,
cues.zh: 最好的编译器、

cues.en: the best editor, the best toolkit, the best development processes
cues.zh: 最好的编辑器、最好的工具包、最好的开发流程

cues.en: will not help you. You will still end up delivering something bad.
cues.zh: 都帮不了你。你最终还是会交付糟糕的东西。

cues.en: So the idea of trying to reduce the garbage coming in, call that design.
cues.zh: 所以，想办法减少进来的垃圾，这就叫设计。

cues.en: Okay. And it's just a general word for just trying to understand what's going on before you start building it.
cues.zh: 好。它只是一个通用说法，指的是在开始构建之前先弄清楚到底在发生什么。

cues.en: So how do we do design right? I think that's why we're all here at this conference to try and figure this out.
cues.zh: 那我们该怎样把设计做对？我想这就是我们齐聚这个大会、想弄明白的事。

cues.en: So there's two parts. The first thing I'm going to take from the agile contribution is getting rapid feedback.
cues.zh: 所以这里分为两部分。我从敏捷开发中借鉴的第一点是获取快速反馈。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 以及

cues.en: doing something and learning from it as fast as possible.
cues.zh: 付诸实践，并以最快的速度从中学习。

cues.en: Don't just take six months to deliver something, try and deliver something in two weeks, or one week, or a few days.
cues.zh: 不要花半年时间才交付成果，试着在两周、一周甚至几天内交付。

cues.en: And then from DDD,
cues.zh: 然后从 DDD 中，

cues.en: I like to think of domain driven designers actually trying to create a shared mental model that everyone is on the same page, everyone is thinking the same way, everyone is using the same words.
cues.zh: 我倾向于认为领域驱动设计旨在创建一个共享的心智模型，让每个人都在同一频道上，用相同的思维方式，使用相同的词汇。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: that shared mental model is also in the code.
cues.zh: 这个共享的心智模型同时也体现在代码中。

cues.en: It's not just in people's heads.
cues.zh: 它不仅存在于人们的脑海中。

cues.en: So here's a little picture
cues.zh: 所以这是一张小图，

cues.en: of the shared mental model, and we have
cues.zh: 展示了共享的心智模型，我们有

cues.en: experts, domain experts, subject matter experts, they're sometimes called. We have product people, we have developers,
cues.zh: 专家、领域专家，有时也叫主题专家。我们有产品人员、开发人员，

cues.en: we have customers, users, whatever you want to call them, stakeholders, everybody.
cues.zh: 我们有客户、用户，随你怎么称呼他们，还有利益相关者，所有人。

cues.en: Everyone involved should be sharing the same mental model. That's
cues.zh: 所有相关人员都应该共享同一个心智模型。这就是

cues.en: my version of domain driven design.
cues.zh: 我理解的领域驱动设计。

cues.en: They're all using the same language, the same concepts.
cues.zh: 他们都在使用相同的语言、相同的概念。

cues.en: And in particular, like I said, the code
cues.zh: 特别是，正如我所说，代码

cues.en: is part of this.
cues.zh: 也是其中的一部分。

cues.en: And the domain model and the code and the documentation all try to be the same thing. Okay. And the common language is in the code as well, not just in people's heads.
cues.zh: 领域模型、代码和文档都试图融为一体。好的。而且通用语言也体现在代码中，而不仅仅是在人们的脑海里。

cues.en: So when I talk to non developers
cues.zh: 所以当我跟非开发人员

cues.en: or even developers and they say, can you really have the code represent the domain?
cues.zh: 甚至开发人员交流，他们会问：代码真的能代表领域吗？

cues.en: This is what people think code looks like, especially non developers.
cues.zh: 这就是人们眼中代码的样子，尤其是对非开发人员来说。

cues.en: And it's like, yeah, this not represent
cues.zh: 就好像，呃，这代表不了

cues.en: anything useful. So
cues.zh: 任何有用的东西。所以

cues.en: the kind of thing I'm talking about, this is the kind of code. I'm going to show you the kind of code
cues.zh: 我要讲的那种东西，就是这种代码。我要向大家展示的代码

cues.en: that I think you should be writing. So you have to try and guess what domain this is. Okay?
cues.zh: 是我认为你们应该去写的。所以你们得试着猜猜这是哪个领域。好吗？

cues.en: So if you can win points by trying to, you know, figure it out.
cues.zh: 如果你能猜出来，就可以拿分，你知道的。

cues.en: Right. So, yes, here we have our game.
cues.zh: 对吧。所以，是的，这就是我们的游戏。

cues.en: And,
cues.zh: 然后，

cues.en: hopefully, you've guessed that it's something to do with a card game.
cues.zh: 希望你们已经猜到它和纸牌游戏有关。

cues.en: And there's something called a suit, there's something called a rank, and there's something called a card, and there's something called a player.
cues.zh: 这里有什么“花色（suit）”、什么“面值（rank）”、什么“牌（card）”，还有什么“玩家（player）”。

cues.en: Now, what's interesting is, I imagine that most of you don't know f. This is f code.
cues.zh: 现在，有趣的是，我猜你们大多数人都不懂 F#。这是 F# 代码。

cues.en: And even though you don't know f, you can probably understand this code
cues.zh: 尽管你们不懂 F#，你们大概也能看懂这段代码

cues.en: because this is about the concepts.
cues.zh: 因为这讲的是概念。

cues.en: So we have our shared language down the side. Right?
cues.zh: 所以我们在旁边有一套共同的语言。对吧？

cues.en: And the way I explain this to non developers... Because I want non developers to read this code, not just programmers.
cues.zh: 我就是这样向非开发人员解释的……因为我想让非开发人员也能读懂这段代码，而不只是程序员。

cues.en: You know, the vertical bar is a choice. So it's a club or a diamond or a spade or a heart.
cues.zh: 你看，竖线代表一种选择。所以它是梅花、方块、黑桃或红桃。

cues.en: The little star means a pair, so a card is a choice of one pick a suit and then pick a rank. You have a list type. And then we have this thing with an arrow.
cues.zh: 小星星代表组合，所以一张牌就是从花色中选一个，再从面值中选一个。你有一个列表类型。然后我们有带箭头的东西。

cues.en: So this is...
cues.zh: 所以这是……

cues.en: To deal
cues.zh: 发牌（deal）

cues.en: is an action. It's not just a noun. It's a verb. It's something you do. And we're going to represent in F or in functional model, we're going to represent this as function. So this says deck arrow,
cues.zh: 是一个动作。它不仅仅是个名词。它是个动词。它是你做的一件事。我们将在 F# 或函数式模型中，把它表示为一个函数。所以这里写的是 deck 箭头，

cues.en: deck star card.
cues.zh: deck 星号 card。

cues.en: Alright? So what does that mean?
cues.zh: 好吧？所以这意味著什么？

cues.en: So here is our function.
cues.zh: 所以这是我们的函数。

cues.en: So functions have inputs and outputs.
cues.zh: 所以函数有输入和输出。

cues.en: And so our deal function, the input is a deck of cards.
cues.zh: 所以对于我们的发牌函数，输入是一副牌。

cues.en: And after we've dealt a card, there is now a new card on the table.
cues.zh: 在我们发出一张牌之后，桌上现在多了一张新牌。

cues.en: And we have a different
cues.zh: 并且我们有了一副

cues.en: deck because in functional programming, everything's immutable.
cues.zh: 不同的牌，因为在函数式编程中，一切都是不可变的。

cues.en: So the deck... You don't mutate
cues.zh: 所以这副牌……你不会去修改

cues.en: the original deck. You create a copy of the original deck with that one card missing.
cues.zh: 原始的牌堆。你创建了原始牌堆的一个副本，只是少了一张牌。

cues.en: So the input is an original deck and the output is a a new deck and a card on the table. So we represent that with deck arrow. That's the input.
cues.zh: 所以输入是原本的牌堆，输出是新牌堆和桌上的一张牌。我们用 deck 箭头来表示这个。那是输入。

cues.en: And then the output is a pair. It's a deck and a card. So that's how we represent an action in our model.
cues.zh: 然后输出是一个二元组。它包含一个牌堆和一张牌。这就是我们在模型中表示动作的方式。

cues.en: Let's look at picking up a card. So there's a card on the table and I have some hand. I have my own cards and I'm gonna pick it up. So the input is my hand and
cues.zh: 我们来看看捡起一张牌。桌上有一张牌，我手里也有一些牌。我有我自己的牌，我要把它捡起来。所以输入是我的手牌和

cues.en: the card on the table.
cues.zh: 桌上的牌。

cues.en: And after I've done the pick up,
cues.zh: 在我完成捡牌动作之后，

cues.en: the card on the table is missing and I have a new hand
cues.zh: 桌上的牌就没有了，我拥有了一副新牌，

cues.en: with a new card in it. So it's a different hand. It's changed.
cues.zh: 里面包含一张新牌。所以这是一副不同的手牌。它变了。

cues.en: So, again, I represent this saying, the input is a pair of things,
cues.zh: 所以，再次地，我这样表示：输入是一对事物，

cues.en: and the output is my new hand.
cues.zh: 而输出是我的新手牌。

cues.en: So this is how we model
cues.zh: 所以这就是我们如何对

cues.en: actions,
cues.zh: 动作、

cues.en: verbs,
cues.zh: 动词、

cues.en: workflows,
cues.zh: 工作流、

cues.en: use cases, stories, whatever you wanna call them. This is how we'd model it in functional programming.
cues.zh: 用例、业务故事——随便你怎么称呼它们——进行建模。这就是我们在函数式编程中对它们进行建模的方式。

cues.en: So here's a question. Do you think this is a reasonable amount of code to write for this domain?
cues.zh: 所以这里有个问题。你觉得为这个领域编写这么多代码合理吗？

cues.en: I would say yes. Basically, we fit the... The whole domain is on one page. It's pretty good. We don't... It's not in 20 different files.
cues.zh: 我会说是的。基本上，我们把……整个领域都在同一页上。这挺好的。我们不用……它不在 20 个不同的文件里。

cues.en: You know, it's actually right there in one page.
cues.zh: 你知道，它其实就在同一页上。

cues.en: Do you think a non programmer could understand this?
cues.zh: 你觉得不懂编程的人能看懂这个吗？

cues.en: And I think, yes.
cues.zh: 我觉得可以。

cues.en: In fact, when I've been doing domain modeling exercises with people, when I have everyone in the room, I have programmers in the room, but I also have the domain experts and the subject matter experts and the product owners in the room. And I'm typing all this stuff out.
cues.zh: 事实上，当我跟别人一起做领域建模练习时，当所有人都在屋里，既有程序员，也有领域专家、主题专家和产品负责人。而我正在把这些东西都敲出来。

cues.en: And someone said, well, is great, but where's the code?
cues.zh: 然后有人说，这挺好，但代码在哪儿？

cues.en: Because this... But it's like this is code. Right?
cues.zh: 因为这……但这就相当于是代码。对吧？

cues.en: Do you think that non programmers... If I'm typing this up on the screen, do you think that non programmers could provide useful feedback?
cues.zh: 你觉得不懂编程的人……如果我在屏幕上敲出这些，你觉得不懂编程的人能提供有用的反馈吗？

cues.en: For example, there's a deliberate mistake. Anyone see what the mistake is?
cues.zh: 比如，这里有个刻意留下的错误。有人看出错在哪了吗？

cues.en: Ace is missing. Right. Now, I I don't think you have to be a programmer to notice that. Right? This is the kind of thing in real in real life I've had people tell me that I forgot something. You know, I didn't... I missed out one of the choices
cues.zh: Ace 漏掉了。没错。现在，我觉得不需要是个程序员也能注意到这点。对吧？现实生活中我经常遇到别人提醒我漏掉了什么。你知道，我没……我漏掉了一个选项

cues.en: because,
cues.zh: 因为，

cues.en: you know... But they can give me that kind of feedback right away.
cues.zh: 你知道……但他们能立刻给我这种反馈。

cues.en: So this thing about rapid feedback
cues.zh: 所以关于快速反馈这一点

cues.en: is really important. Now in agile,
cues.zh: 真的很重要。现在在敏捷开发中，

cues.en: the idea is to get feedback
cues.zh: 其理念是通过快速原型、通过最小可行性产品、通过所有这些不同的说法，

cues.en: in weeks or even better in days by having a rapid prototype, by having a minimal viral product, by having all these different words.
cues.zh: 在几周甚至几天内获得反馈。

cues.en: Wouldn't it be great if you could get feedback in minutes rather than days?
cues.zh: 如果能几分钟就拿到反馈，而不是等上几天，那岂不是很好？

cues.en: That would be awesome.

cues.en: which is a little easier to read for for non technical people.
cues.zh: 这对于非技术人员来说更容易阅读一点。

cues.en: So the same thing.
cues.zh: 所以是一样的。

cues.en: That's nice and readable.
cues.zh: 这就很好读。

cues.en: Right. What about
cues.zh: 对吧。那

cues.en: simple values and constrained values?
cues.zh: 简单值和受限值呢？

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: as someone pointed out, we really should avoid primitive obsession.
cues.zh: 正如某人所指出的，我们确实应该避免基本类型偏执。

cues.en: We shouldn't use ints and floats and bools and strings in our domain because that's not what people use in real world. Okay?
cues.zh: 我们不应该在领域模型中使用 int、float、bool 和 string，因为现实世界中人们用的不是这些。好吗？

cues.en: I was once at a... I want to do... When I was younger and I was modeling something and I said, well, is this an integer or is it a float?
cues.zh: 我曾经在……我想做……在我更年轻的时候，我在做建模，我说，嗯，这是整数还是浮点数？

cues.en: And they said,
cues.zh: 然后他们说，

cues.en: Is float something to do with water? You know? They did not know what I was talking about, which is fair enough. Why should they? They're not a they're not a programmer. So don't use the word float. Don't use the word integer. Use
cues.zh: float 是跟水有关的东西吗？你知道吗？他们根本不知道我在说什么，这很合情合理。他们为什么要知道？他们又不是程序员。所以不要用 float 这个词。不要用 integer 这个词。要用

cues.en: payment amount or,
cues.zh: 支付金额，或者，

cues.en: you know,
cues.zh: 你知道的，

cues.en: product number or whatever it is. Right?
cues.zh: 产品编号之类的事物。对吧？

cues.en: And on top of that, not only should we not use primitive types, but almost always,
cues.zh: 此外，我们不仅不该使用基本类型，而且几乎总是，

cues.en: integers and strings
cues.zh: 整数和字符串

cues.en: have some sort of constraints.
cues.zh: 会有某种约束。

cues.en: It's very unusual for a string to allow a string to have a million characters in it or to allow an integer. Can you, you know, can you have integers which are 4,000,000,000?
cues.zh: 字符串允许自己有一百万个字符，或者允许整数任意取值，这都很不寻常。你说，能有 4,000,000,000 这样的整数吗？

cues.en: I mean, it's really... Maybe, but it's really unusual.
cues.zh: 我是说，这真的……也许吧，但真的很不寻常。

cues.en: Normally, there's some sort of constraints on your things. So for example, an email address. You know, it can't be empty. It has to have some sort of pattern matching like an at sign. If you have customer ID, which is an int,
cues.zh: 通常，你的数据会有某种约束。比如电子邮件地址，它不能为空，必须符合某种模式匹配，比如包含 @ 符号。如果你有一个客户 ID，它是个 int，

cues.en: it's probably not any int. It's probably a positive integer. Right? So there's some sort of constraint.
cues.zh: 它大概不是任意 int，而很可能是正整数。对吧？所以是有某种约束的。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: email addresses are not strings.
cues.zh: 电子邮件地址不是字符串。

cues.en: Customer IDs are not ints. I mean, another way to think about it. If you think about an int, like a customer ID, the reason it's not an int is because you can't take the square root of it. Can you add two customer IDs and get another customer ID? Can you multiply it by five? It doesn't make any sense. Right? So they might be represented by ints, they're not actually ints in the domain.
cues.zh: 客户 ID 不是 int。我是说，换个角度想。如果你把客户 ID 当作一个 int，它之所以不是 int，是因为你不能对它开平方。你能把两个客户 ID 相加得到另一个客户 ID 吗？能把它乘以五吗？这毫无意义。对吧？所以它们可能用 int 表示，但在领域里并不是真正的 int。

cues.en: So what we do is we use wrapper types to keep them distinct.
cues.zh: 所以我们用包装类型把它们区分开。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: here's two wrapper types. This is the f sharp way of doing a wrapper type. We just put a email of string. So it's wrapping a string. Custom ID of int is wrapping an int. Right? So wrapping a string and wrapping int. So it's very simple. One line to do that.
cues.zh: 这里有两个包装类型。这是 F# 里做包装类型的方式。我们只要写一个 email of string，就是在包装一个字符串。Custom ID of int 是在包装一个 int。对吧？所以就是包装字符串和包装 int。非常简单，一行就能做到。

cues.en: So here's two wrapped types. An email address wraps a string and a phone number wraps a string. But because we've got wrappers around them, they are now distinct types. And that means you can't ever get an email address mixed up with a phone number.
cues.zh: 所以这里有两个包装类型。一个电子邮件地址包装了一个字符串，一个电话号码也包装了一个字符串。但因为我们给它们加上了包装，它们现在是不同的类型了。这意味着你绝不会把电子邮件地址和电话号码弄混。

cues.en: And let's say we have a customer ID and an order ID, and they both wrap in your database. But they're not the same type. They're different types.
cues.zh: 假设我们有一个客户 ID 和一个订单 ID，它们在你的数据库底层都包装自字符串。但它们不是同一种类型。它们是不同的类型。

cues.en: They can't be mixed up. You should never pass an order ID to somebody that's expecting a customer ID. It just doesn't make any sense.
cues.zh: 它们不可能被混淆。你绝不应该把一个订单 ID 传给期望得到客户 ID 的地方。这根本说不通。

cues.en: So model them as distinct types always.
cues.zh: 所以，永远要把它们建模为不同的类型。

cues.en: So you get clear domain modeling, and it also eliminates one kind of bug where you accidentally mix them up. You pass them in the wrong order or something.
cues.zh: 这样你就能获得清晰的领域建模，还能消灭那种不小心把它们搞混的Bug。比如以错误的顺序传递参数之类的。

cues.en: Okay. So now let's look at how we create one of these things. Let's say I want to create an email address, and I've got a string.
cues.zh: 好的。现在让我们来看看如何创建这些东西。比方说我想创建一个电子邮件地址，我手头有一个字符串。

cues.en: Now if the string contains the at sign,
cues.zh: 如果这个字符串包含“@”符号，

cues.en: then I'm gonna take the string, and I'm gonna wrap it up in the email address.
cues.zh: 那我就把这个字符串拿来，把它包装成一个电子邮件地址。

cues.en: That's good. What happens if it doesn't contain the at sign?
cues.zh: 这很好。如果它不包含“@”符号会怎么样？

cues.en: What should I do?
cues.zh: 我该怎么办？

cues.en: Should I return null?
cues.zh: 我是不是该返回空值？

cues.en: No. Should I throw an exception?
cues.zh: 不。我是不是该抛出一个异常？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不。

cues.en: So what can I do? What can what can I return?
cues.zh: 那我能做什么？我能——我能返回什么？

cues.en: You know, I can't return an email address because it's not a valid email address. Nothing. Nothing. Right.
cues.zh: 你知道的，我不能返回一个电子邮件地址，因为它不是一个合法的电子邮件地址。什么都没有。什么都没有。对吧。

cues.en: Exactly.
cues.zh: 完全正确。

cues.en: So one of the things if you if you throw if you return null or you would throw an exception or something if you look at the signature it says you give me a string and I'll give you an email address and that is a lie.
cues.zh: 所以其中有一点，如果你——如果你返回空值，或者你抛出异常之类的，如果你看它的签名，上面写着你给我一个字符串，我还你一个电子邮件地址，而那是个谎言。

cues.en: That is wrong.
cues.zh: 那是错的。

cues.en: So it's a deceptive
cues.zh: 所以这是一个极具误导性的

cues.en: piece of information.
cues.zh: 信息片段。

cues.en: So, yes, what I'm gonna do is return something or nothing just like we did with the optional thing.
cues.zh: 所以，是的，我要做的是返回某个东西或者什么都不返回，就像我们处理可选类型（optional）时那样。

cues.en: And that's much better.
cues.zh: 而且这要好得多。

cues.en: So if you look at the signature, it now says, you give me a string,
cues.zh: 所以如果你看一下签名，它现在写着，你给我一个字符串，

cues.en: and I might give you back an email address. Maybe.
cues.zh: 我可能会还给你一个电子邮箱地址。也许吧。

cues.en: If you give me a good string.
cues.zh: 如果你给我的字符串没问题的话。

cues.en: So this is now... This is not a lie. This is much clearer. This is better documentation too. This is now,
cues.zh: 所以这现在……这不再是个谎言了。这清晰多了。这也是更好的文档。这现在是，

cues.en: you know, a
cues.zh: 你知道的，一种

cues.en: self documenting code, better than the other one.
cues.zh: 自文档化代码，比之前那个更好。

cues.en: And we can do the same thing. Let's say we want to have strings that are 50 characters long. So we create a wrapper type for them and then we create a special constructor for them.
cues.zh: 我们也可以做同样的事情。假设我们想要长度为 50 个字符的字符串。于是我们为它们创建一个包装类型，然后为它们创建一个特殊的构造函数。

cues.en: And if it's less than 50, that's good. And if not,
cues.zh: 如果小于 50，那就没问题。如果不是，

cues.en: then that's bad.
cues.zh: 那就不行。

cues.en: And if we look at the signature, it says, you give me a normal string and I might give you back a string 50 if it's good.
cues.zh: 如果我们看签名，它上面写着，你给我一个普通字符串，如果符合要求，我可能会返回一个 string 50 给你。

cues.en: So this kind of validation
cues.zh: 所以这种验证

cues.en: is normally just done at the edges of your program.
cues.zh: 通常只在你的程序边缘进行。

cues.en: When you get data coming in from a JSON thing or from whatever, you have to validate it. But once it's validated,
cues.zh: 当你有数据从 JSON 传入或其他任何地方传入时，你必须对其进行验证。但一旦验证通过，

cues.en: once you've got your string 50 or your email address, it's immutable.
cues.zh: 一旦你拿到了 string 50 或电子邮箱地址，它就是不可变的。

cues.en: So it can never change,
cues.zh: 所以它永远不会改变，

cues.en: which means you never have to validate it ever again.
cues.zh: 这意味着你再也不用验证它了。

cues.en: So you never have to do any kind of defensive programming in your core domain code. You never have to check for null. You never have to check that something's valid. Because once it's been validated at the edge,
cues.zh: 因此，你永远不需要在核心领域代码中做任何防御性编程。你再也不用检查 null。你再也不用检查某个东西是否有效。因为一旦它在边缘被验证过，

cues.en: you can pass it around
cues.zh: 你就可以放心地把它

cues.en: in full confidence that it can never go wrong. So that's one of the nice things about this.
cues.zh: 传递到各处，完全不用担心会出问题。所以这是这方法的优点之一。

cues.en: Okay. Here's something which is which is a problem.
cues.zh: 好吧。这里有个问题。

cues.en: Can you really have,
cues.zh: 你真的能往

cues.en: items in your shopping cart or your shopping bars?
cues.zh: 购物车或商品栏里放这么多东西吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不能。

cues.en: This is probably a bug
cues.zh: 这很可能是一个 Bug，

cues.en: because the person who wrote this ecommerce site probably used an integer
cues.zh: 因为写这个电商网站的人大概是用了一个整型

cues.en: to represent the quantity.
cues.zh: 来表示数量。

cues.en: Right? And you hear stories of, you know, things overflowing to minus one or minus 32 k or something create... You know, this should never happen. You should never be able to order that many things.
cues.zh: 对吧？你经常听说，你知道的，数值溢出变成负一或负三万二千之类的……你知道的，这本就不该发生。你绝不应该能订购那么多东西。

cues.en: So that's because they didn't do domain modeling.
cues.zh: 所以这是因为他们没有做领域建模。

cues.en: So the right answer is to create a type, a wrapper type.
cues.zh: 所以正确的做法是创建一个类型，一个包装类型。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: to be honest, when I've done ecommerce sites, I have never bothered to do this
cues.zh: 老实说，当我开发电商网站时，我以前从懒得这么做，

cues.en: before because it's a lot of work creating these wrapper types.
cues.zh: 因为创建这些包装类型太费劲了。

cues.en: You know, creating a new type just for this domain or just for this little piece of code is not something that people do generally.
cues.zh: 你知道的，仅仅为了这个领域或这小段代码就创建一个新类型，通常大家不会这么做。

cues.en: Because it's like I say, it's a of work. But if it's one line of code,
cues.zh: 因为就像我说的，这工作量不小。但如果只需一行代码，

cues.en: it's a lot easier. So if your language makes it easy to do, you'd like to do it much more.
cues.zh: 那就轻松多了。所以如果你的语言让这变得很容易，你就会更乐意去做了。

cues.en: Hey. Let's look at the instructor.
cues.zh: 嘿。我们来看看这个构造函数。

cues.en: So if it's greater than zero, less than 99,
cues.zh: 所以如果它大于零且小于 99，

cues.en: that's good. And if it isn't, it's bad.
cues.zh: 那就行。如果不是，就不行。

cues.en: Then we look at the signature. It says, you give me integer,
cues.zh: 然后我们看签名。上面写着，你给我一个整数，

cues.en: and I might or might not give you back an order line quantity.
cues.zh: 我可能会也可能不会返回给你一个订单行数量。

cues.en: Now what's interesting about this is that zero is not a valid value. It has to be greater than zero.
cues.zh: 这里有趣的是，零不是一个有效值。它必须大于零。

cues.en: So when you have the one of those minus buttons
cues.zh: 所以当你拥有其中一个减号按钮

cues.en: and you're down your two and you take away one that's one, you take away another one, it goes down to zero,
cues.zh: 你原本有两件，拿走一件剩下一件，再拿走一件，就变成零了，

cues.en: you can't make one of these things.
cues.zh: 你就不能再造出这种东西了。

cues.en: So what that means is that when you're coding your UI,
cues.zh: 所以这意味着，当你在编写界面代码时，

cues.en: or your back end or whatever,
cues.zh: 或者编写后端以及其他任何代码时，

cues.en: you are forced to deal with the case when it goes down to zero. You can't accidentally forget about it.
cues.zh: 你被迫去处理它归零的情况。你不会不小心把它漏掉。

cues.en: So this is the idea where, you know, it forces you to think about that situation
cues.zh: 所以这就是那个理念，你知道的，它迫使你去思考那种情况，

cues.en: because you don't actually have a valid quantity at that point. So you... What are you gonna do? I don't know. You're probably gonna remove it from the shopping cart.
cues.zh: 因为在那时你其实已经没有一个有效的数量了。所以你……你要怎么办？我不知道。你可能会把它从购物车里移除。

cues.en: But whatever the answer is, you're gonna have to think about it. You can't just forget about it, you know, and cause a bug.
cues.zh: 但不管解决方案是什么，你都得去考虑它。你不能就这么置之不理，然后引发一个Bug。

cues.en: So if we go back to our contacts,
cues.zh: 所以如果我们回到我们的联系人，

cues.en: here's what we had originally.
cues.zh: 这是我们最初的代码。

cues.en: So the first thing we did is make an option.
cues.zh: 所以我们做的第一件事是创建了一个可选类型。

cues.en: And then the second thing we did is we created all these constrained types for all these different choices.
cues.zh: 然后我们做的第二件事是，为所有这些不同的选项创建了所有这些受限类型。

cues.en: Right? So all... It's looking better already.
cues.zh: 对吧？所以所有……看起来已经好多了。

cues.en: The next thing is we need... You know, if you're a domain driven design person, you'll recognize this is an entity. So we need to add
cues.zh: 接下来我们需要……你知道的，如果你懂领域驱动设计，你会认出这是一个实体。所以我们需要添加

cues.en: an entity ID.
cues.zh: 一个实体ID。

cues.en: And notice that I'm not... It's not an int. It's something called a customer ID,
cues.zh: 请注意，我用的不是……它不是int。它是一个叫做customer ID的东西，

cues.en: special to customers or contact. It really should be a contact ID, I guess. And then
cues.zh: 专门针对客户或联系人。我想它其实应该叫contact ID。然后

cues.en: here's our two
cues.zh: 这里是我们的两个

cues.en: things which really should be separate.
cues.zh: 其实应该分开的东西。

cues.en: Well, can just... Rather than having them in one big structure, can just pull them out into two separate structures.
cues.zh: 好吧，其实可以……与其把它们放在一个大结构里，不如把它们拆成两个独立的结构。

cues.en: And one of the nice things about
cues.zh: 其中一个好处就是

cues.en: having the data separate from behavior is that this kind of pulling things apart and putting them back together again
cues.zh: 把数据和行为分离开来，这种把东西拆开再重新组合的操作

cues.en: is really easy to do
cues.zh: 做起来非常容易

cues.en: because,
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: there's no behavior. So, you know,
cues.zh: 里面没有行为。所以你看，

cues.en: refactoring is very, very easy.
cues.zh: 重构变得非常非常简单。

cues.en: Right. So that's that. Now what about this last thing here? Where is it? This email verify flag. What we're gonna do with that?
cues.zh: 好，那就这样。那最后这个东西呢？在哪？这个邮箱验证标志。我们拿它怎么办？

cues.en: So let's talk about getting rid of flags altogether.
cues.zh: 那我们来聊聊怎么彻底干掉标志。

cues.en: What we're going to do is replace flags with choices.
cues.zh: 我们要用选择来代替标志。

cues.en: So here's our situation.
cues.zh: 所以情况是这样的。

cues.en: We have this flag,
cues.zh: 我们有这个标志，

cues.en: and we have some business rules. And it says if the email is changed,
cues.zh: 还有一些业务规则。上面说如果邮箱改了，

cues.en: that verify flag has to be set to false.
cues.zh: 那个验证标志就必须设为 false。

cues.en: Because who knows? You know, you can set it to anything.
cues.zh: 因为谁知道呢？你知道的，你把它设成什么都行。

cues.en: And also,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: if you do want to set it to true, you have to use a special verification service that compares... You know, that checks the email hash and all that other stuff. You can't just set it to true because that's a security issue. You have to go through the special verification service. So that's a business rule.
cues.zh: 如果你确实想把它设为 true，你必须使用一个特殊的验证服务来进行比对……你知道的，就是检查邮箱哈希值以及其他那些东西。你不能直接把它设为 true，因为这涉及安全问题。你必须通过那个特殊的验证服务。所以这就是一条业务规则。

cues.en: Can we enforce the business rule in the design
cues.zh: 我们能在设计中强制执行这条业务规则吗，

cues.en: without having some logic somewhere?
cues.zh: 而不需要在某处写一堆逻辑？

cues.en: And the answer is yes, we can.
cues.zh: 答案是肯定的，我们可以。

cues.en: So as it stands, anyone can set it to true. It's a security problem, and it's it's just bad. It doesn't communicate the issue.
cues.zh: 所以目前的情况是，任何人都能把它设为 true。这是个安全问题，而且这真的很糟糕。它没能表达出这个问题的关键。

cues.en: So here's what we're going do. We're going to create another wrapper type.
cues.zh: 接下来我们要这么做：我们要创建另一个包装类型。

cues.en: We're going wrap an email address, and we're going to call it a verified email address.
cues.zh: 我们要把一个电子邮件地址包装起来，称之为已验证的电子邮件地址。

cues.en: So we have a wrapper around a wrapper.
cues.zh: 所以我们得到了一个“套娃”式的包装。

cues.en: And this is one of my favorite
cues.zh: 这也是我最喜欢的

cues.en: principles,
cues.zh: 原则之一，

cues.en: which is there's no problem that can't be solved by wrapping it in another type. We're going to see that.
cues.zh: 那就是：没有什么问题是用另一个包装类型解决不了的。我们马上就会看到这一点。

cues.en: So by by doing this, what we've said is that a verified email address is not the same as a normal email address. Right? The whole thing is is a is a distinct type. Just like a shuffle deck is not the same thing as normal deck. We've created a special concept
cues.zh: 所以通过这样做，我们表达的意思是：已验证的电子邮件地址和普通的电子邮件地址是不一样的。对吧？整个东西是一个截然不同的类型。就像洗过的牌和没洗过的牌不一样。我们在业务领域中

cues.en: in the domain.
cues.zh: 创建了一个特殊的概念。

cues.en: And then we're going to have a verification service. Now, service
cues.zh: 然后我们将拥有一个验证服务。现在，服务

cues.en: is a function
cues.zh: 其实就是一个函数，

cues.en: which has two inputs and one output. And the input is an email address
cues.zh: 它有两个输入和一个输出。输入是一个电子邮件地址

cues.en: and a verification hash of some kind.
cues.zh: 和某种验证哈希。

cues.en: So you give me the email address,
cues.zh: 所以你给我电子邮件地址，

cues.en: and I'm gonna give you back a verified email
cues.zh: 我就会还给你一个已验证的电子邮件，

cues.en: maybe
cues.zh: 也许吧，

cues.en: because the hash might not match up or whatever. I mean, there's various reasons it might not work. It's very clear that it might not work sometimes. So you have to deal with that.
cues.zh: 因为哈希可能匹配不上或者怎样。我的意思是，它可能不成功的原因有很多。很明显，它有时就是会失败。所以你必须处理这种情况。

cues.en: Okay? So I might give you back a verified email.
cues.zh: 好吗？所以我可能会还给你一个已验证的电子邮件。

cues.en: Okay? So that's the verification
cues.zh: 好吗？这就是验证

cues.en: function.
cues.zh: 函数。

cues.en: And then here's the cool bit. We take this contact information and we change it into a choice.
cues.zh: 接下来是酷炫的部分。我们把这个联系信息转换成一个二选一的选择。

cues.en: We say it's either a choice between the unverified email and a verified email. So this flag has disappeared.
cues.zh: 我们说它要么是未验证的邮箱，要么是已验证的邮箱。所以这个标志位就消失了。

cues.en: Unverified
cues.zh: 未验证

cues.en: or
cues.zh: 或

cues.en: verified.
cues.zh: 已验证。

cues.en: Now in the unverified case, the information that goes along with it is just a normal
cues.zh: 那么在未验证的情况下，与之对应的信息只是一个普通的

cues.en: email address.
cues.zh: 电子邮件地址。

cues.en: So anybody can set it to be unverified. All I need is any old email address. To set it to the verified case,
cues.zh: 所以任何人都可以把它设为未验证。我只需要随便一个旧邮箱地址。要把它设为已验证的情况，

cues.en: I have to have the verified email. That's the thing I need to have
cues.zh: 我必须拥有已验证的邮箱。那才是我需要拥有的东西

cues.en: to put it into the verified case.
cues.zh: 才能把它放入已验证的情况。

cues.en: Where do I get one of these verified emails from?
cues.zh: 我从哪里获得这样的已验证邮箱呢？

cues.en: I have to get it from the verification service.
cues.zh: 我必须从验证服务那里获取。

cues.en: Right? So the... It may not... What I typically do is make the constructor private or something so that nobody else can create one of these things except the verifications.
cues.zh: 对吧？所以……它可能不……我通常的做法是把构造函数设为私有之类的，这样除了验证服务之外，其他任何人都无法创建这样的东西。

cues.en: But by doing that now, just like the business rule says, I have to get one from the verification service. The only person who can create one of these things.
cues.zh: 但这样一来，正如业务规则所说，我必须从验证服务那里获取一个。只有验证服务才能创建这样的东西。

cues.en: So that's that business rule. I I have to go through the verification service to get a verified email. So in that... For that case to be true. Okay?
cues.zh: 所以这就是那条业务规则。我必须通过验证服务才能获得一个已验证邮箱。所以在那个……那种情况下才成立。明白吗？

cues.en: So by replacing the boolean with a choice,
cues.zh: 所以通过用选择来替代布尔值，

cues.en: it's first of all clearer. And secondly, I've actually enforced those business rules.
cues.zh: 首先它更清晰。其次，我实际上强制执行了那些业务规则。

cues.en: I think it's amazing.
cues.zh: 我觉得这太棒了。

cues.en: Alright. So to create that case, you have to go have a verified email.
cues.zh: 好的。所以要创建那种情况，你必须拥有一个已验证邮箱。

cues.en: And to create a verified email, you have to go through the service. So the business rules are automatically enforced.
cues.zh: 而要创建一个已验证邮箱，你必须通过该服务。所以业务规则被自动强制执行了。

cues.en: So this is a really nice way of doing it. So I'm modeling the domain more accurately and I'm also getting my business rules.
cues.zh: 所以这是一种非常好的做法。我既能更准确地建模领域，又能实现我的业务规则。

cues.en: Right. So if we go back to our challenge,
cues.zh: 好。那么如果我们回到之前的挑战，

cues.en: we started off with one thing. We now have a whole bunch of things. We have an email address and a verified email and a contact information and a personal name and a contact and a verification. We have a whole bunch of things that we didn't have at the beginning.
cues.zh: 我们一开始只有一样东西。现在我们有了一大堆东西。我们有电子邮件地址、已验证的邮箱、联系信息、个人姓名、联系方式以及验证状态。我们拥有了一大堆一开始没有的东西。

cues.en: So what's good about this is a lot of the stuff
cues.zh: 所以好的一点是，

cues.en: that we had at the beginning are now solved.
cues.zh: 我们最初面临的很多问题现在都解决了。

cues.en: Right? Which values are optional? Why you have this optional
cues.zh: 对吧？哪些值是可选的？为什么要有这个可选的

cues.en: concept?
cues.zh: 概念？

cues.en: What are the constraints?
cues.zh: 约束条件是什么？

cues.en: Well, we have something called a string 50. We have something called an email address. It's not just strings anymore.
cues.zh: 嗯，我们有类似于长度50的字符串。我们有类似于电子邮件地址的东西。它不再仅仅是字符串了。

cues.en: Which fields are linked?
cues.zh: 哪些字段是关联的？

cues.en: By breaking them into separate groups, it's much more obvious.
cues.zh: 通过将它们拆分成独立的组，这就明显多了。

cues.en: And is the domain logic clear? Yes, it is. Unlike that boolean flag,
cues.zh: 而且领域逻辑清晰吗？是的，很清晰。不像那个布尔标志，

cues.en: it's crystal clear that there's these things called unverified
cues.zh: 这里存在未验证

cues.en: and verified.
cues.zh: 和已验证的概念，一目了然。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: what's also cool about this is that the ubiquitous language, the common language, is evolving
cues.zh: 这其中很棒的一点是，通用语言，也就是日常用语，正在随着

cues.en: along with the design. We started off with one thing, and we have all these new things. But this is not... I wouldn't say this is more complex, because these are actual real words that real people use. They would talk about something called a personal name. They talk about something called verified email and a normal email. These are words in the domain.
cues.zh: 设计一起演进。我们从一个事物开始，现在有了所有这些新事物。但这并不是……我不会说这变得更复杂了，因为这些都是现实中人们会使用的真实词汇。他们会讨论诸如个人姓名之类的事情。他们会讨论已验证的邮箱和普通邮箱。这些都是该领域中的词汇。

cues.en: So we're actually just representing the domain better.
cues.zh: 所以我们其实只是在更好地表达这个领域。

cues.en: We're not making it more complicated. We're actually... If anything, we're making it more clear.
cues.zh: 我们并没有把它变得更复杂。实际上……如果非要说的话，我们让它更清晰了。

cues.en: And of course, this is compileable code. This is not UML diagram.
cues.zh: 当然，这是可编译的代码，不是 UML 图。

cues.en: Now the other thing in in Eric's book, talks about refactoring
cues.zh: Eric 的书里还谈到了重构

cues.en: towards deeper insight, which means when you learn something about the domain,
cues.zh: 通过重构获得更深层的理解，也就是说，当你了解了领域中的某些内容，

cues.en: often that opens up a whole new way of thinking about certain things
cues.zh: 这通常会带来一种全新的思考方式

cues.en: that you didn't really... That you weren't really aware of before. So, for example, we just created this thing called a verified email to solve that particular problem.
cues.zh: 去理解一些你之前并没有真正……并没有真正意识到的事情。比如，我们刚创建了一个叫作“已验证邮箱”的东西，来解决那个特定问题。

cues.en: But once we have this concept called a verified email,
cues.zh: 但一旦我们有了“已验证邮箱”这个概念，

cues.en: you might find all sorts of other uses for it in the domain.
cues.zh: 你可能会发现它在这个领域中还有各种各样的用途。

cues.en: Right?
cues.zh: 对吧？

cues.en: So this new... Often, like I say, you find a new concept
cues.zh: 所以这个新概念……通常，正如我所说，你会发现一个新概念，

cues.en: and then you say, well, okay, this rule, we have a business rule that we didn't think about. This says you have to send parcel to recess only to verified emails.
cues.zh: 然后你会说，好吧，这条规则，我们之前没考虑到一条业务规则。也就是说，只有已验证的邮箱才能接收密码重置邮件。

cues.en: Now before,
cues.zh: 而在此之前，

cues.en: we would have something where we check the flag and only if it's set to true do we actually do the thing. Again, we could easily make a mistake and
cues.zh: 我们可能会检查一个标志位，只有它为 true 时才真正执行操作。这样一来，我们很容易犯错，

cues.en: forget the business rule. But if we, with this new thing called a verified email, we just say sending a password reset, it needs a verified email.
cues.zh: 忘记这条业务规则。但有了“已验证邮箱”这个新概念，我们只需说，发送密码重置邮件需要一个已验证邮箱。

cues.en: So our domain modelling is actually more... Is now self documenting. To send a password reset you need a verified email. Okay? I don't have to write a unit test for it.
cues.zh: 这样一来，我们的领域建模实际上更加……现在变得自文档化了。要发送密码重置邮件，你需要一个已验证邮箱。明白吗？我不需要为此编写单元测试。

cues.en: I don't have to check any billion flags.
cues.zh: 我不用检查几十亿个标志位。

cues.en: You know, self documenting and it's a compile time unit test.
cues.zh: 你看，自文档化，而且它就是一个编译期单元测试。

cues.en: Alright.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: One more thing. So
cues.zh: 还有一件事。那么

cues.en: let's say that times change and we add something called an address, a postal address to our contact. So we have an email and an address.
cues.zh: 假设时代变了，我们给联系人加了个叫地址的东西，一个邮政地址。这样我们就有邮箱和地址。

cues.en: And we have a new business rule that you have to have... A contact must have an email address or
cues.zh: 而且我们有一条新的业务规则，你必须要有……一个联系人必须有一个邮箱地址或者

cues.en: a postal address. There must be one way of contacting you. Okay? At least one way of contact.
cues.zh: 一个邮政地址。必须有一种联系到你的方式。明白吗？至少一种联系方式。

cues.en: Now this design as it stands,
cues.zh: 现在这个设计按现状来看，

cues.en: does it meet that requirement?
cues.zh: 它满足那个要求吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不满足。

cues.en: Because as it stands, both are... Both fields are required. Right? Things are always required unless you tell they're optional. Okay. Well, I'll make them both optional.
cues.zh: 因为按现状，两个都……两个字段都是必填的。对吧？字段默认都是必填的，除非你声明它们是可选的。好吧。那我就把它们都改成可选的。

cues.en: It doesn't work either. Right? Because they're both missing.
cues.zh: 这样也不行。对吧？因为可能两个都缺失。

cues.en: So our problem is how do we model the facts... How do we model this business law? Well, we could say, well, let them both be missing and I'll have some special validation logic somewhere checks if they're both missing and throws an exception. It's like, no. We're not gonna do that. We're gonna try and model it in the domain.
cues.zh: 所以我们的问题是：如何对事实建模……如何对这条业务规则建模？我们本可以说，让它们两个都可以缺失，然后在某处写点特殊的校验逻辑，检查它们是否都缺失，如果都缺失就抛异常。这不行。我们不打算那么做。我们要试着在领域模型里把它建模出来。

cues.en: Can can we do that?
cues.zh: 我们能这么做吗？

cues.en: The answer is yes. Of course we can. Right. So
cues.zh: 答案是肯定的。我们当然能。对吧。那么

cues.en: a great phrase is make illegal states unrepresentable.
cues.zh: 有一句很棒的话：让非法状态无法被表示。

cues.en: So rather than letting people do something and then having validation logic
cues.zh: 所以与其让人做出某种操作，然后再用校验逻辑

cues.en: or special code checks, that's a bad thing. Just don't let it happen in the first place. Okay? So how can we do that? Here's our business rule.
cues.zh: 或者特殊代码去检查，那是糟糕的做法。一开始就别让它发生。明白吗？那我们怎么做呢？这就是我们的业务规则。

cues.en: So if you think about it, that means you can have an email address or a postal address
cues.zh: 仔细想想，这意味着你可以有电子邮箱，或者邮寄地址，

cues.en: or both.
cues.zh: 或者两者都有。

cues.en: Right? That's what the business rule. Now I'm using the word or.
cues.zh: 对吧？这就是业务规则。注意，我这里用了“或者”这个词。

cues.en: There's a clue. How am I gonna model this?
cues.zh: 这就是线索。那我该怎么建模呢？

cues.en: There's three possibilities.
cues.zh: 一共有三种可能性。

cues.en: Okay?
cues.zh: 明白吧？

cues.en: Well, I'm gonna model it like this.
cues.zh: 好，我会这样来建模：

cues.en: Email only or
cues.zh: 仅邮箱，或者

cues.en: address only or both.
cues.zh: 仅地址，或者两者都有。

cues.en: Right? So by modeling it this way... And then I, you know, I stick it in my contact. By modeling it this way,
cues.zh: 对吧？通过这样建模……然后把它放到 contact 里。通过这种建模方式，

cues.en: there's only three possibilities.
cues.zh: 就只有这三种可能性。

cues.en: So it's self documenting.
cues.zh: 所以它是自文档化的。

cues.en: I don't have to have any special code that checks the the the fourth case because there isn't a fourth case. I literally cannot compile
cues.zh: 我不需要写专门的代码去检查第四种情况，因为根本不存在第四种情况。在编译器层面，

cues.en: the fourth case where they're both missing.
cues.zh: 两者皆无的第四种情况根本无法通过编译。

cues.en: I don't have to write a unit test for it. It literally cannot happen. It is not possible for me to write bad code.
cues.zh: 我也不需要为此写单元测试。它根本不可能发生。我绝不可能写出有 bug 的代码。

cues.en: And it's good if if I'm a new developer and I'm coming onto your team
cues.zh: 这样做的好处是，如果我是个刚加入你们团队的新人，

cues.en: and I'm trying to understand what are the business rules,
cues.zh: 想搞清楚业务规则究竟是什么，

cues.en: I don't have to look at documentation.
cues.zh: 我都不需要去看文档。

cues.en: I don't have to ask somebody what are the business rules for emails or whatever.
cues.zh: 我也不用去问别人关于邮箱什么的业务规则到底怎样。

cues.en: I can look at the code.
cues.zh: 我只要看代码就行。

cues.en: The code is really, really explicit. It's kind of ugly. I want... I don't want to say it's beautiful code. It's ugly, but it's explicit.
cues.zh: 代码表达得极其直白。虽然有点丑，我不想说这是漂亮的代码，它确实丑，但非常明确。

cues.en: You're not going to make a mistake.
cues.zh: 你绝不会搞错。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 对吧。

cues.en: So there's the idea of... And try to encode the requirements in the type as much as possible. Now you can't always do that. The rules of poker, for example, you know, like with a card game, you can encode a lot of the stuff, but you can't encode everything.
cues.zh: 所以核心思想就是……尽量把业务需求编码到类型系统中。当然，你不可能每次都做到。比如扑克牌的规则，在这种纸牌游戏里，你可以把很多规则编码进去，但不可能把所有东西都放进去。

cues.en: But you can encode more than you think.
cues.zh: 但你能编码的东西比你想象的多。

cues.en: You can at least get all the big concepts down and the concept of dealing and picking up cards and, you know, all that stuff.
cues.zh: 你至少可以把所有重要概念都记下来，比如发牌、捡牌之类的概念。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: static types are almost as awesome as this.
cues.zh: 静态类型几乎和这个一样酷。

cues.en: A cat on a unicorn.
cues.zh: 一只骑在独角兽上的猫。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 对。

cues.en: So, communication is two way.
cues.zh: 所以，沟通是双向的。

cues.en: It's okay
cues.zh: 可以

cues.en: to push back.
cues.zh: 提出反对意见。

cues.en: A contact
cues.zh: 一个联系人

cues.en: must have an email or postal address. You might say, well, that's actually really a bad thing because
cues.zh: 必须有电子邮件或邮寄地址。你可能会说，这其实是个坏事，因为

cues.en: that might not be... You know, it's hard to implement.
cues.zh: 那可能不……你知道，很难实现。

cues.en: So let's change it to be a contact must have at least one way of being contacted.
cues.zh: 所以我们改成：一个联系人必须至少有一种联系方式。

cues.en: So that's better.
cues.zh: 这样更好。

cues.en: So instead of having both things, we'll say you've got one way of being contacted. So here's all the different ways we can contact you. We can contact you by email or address or whatever.
cues.zh: 所以不是两者都要有，而是说你有了一种联系方式。这里列出了我们能联系到你的各种方式——可以通过电子邮件、地址或其他方式联系你。

cues.en: And then we go back and we say, you've got a primary way of being contacted and a secondary way. The primary way is acquired and the secondary way is optional.
cues.zh: 然后我们回过头来说，你有一个主要联系方式和一个次要联系方式。主要方式是必需的，次要方式是可选的。

cues.en: So this is a better design.
cues.zh: 所以这是更好的设计。

cues.en: Okay. This is a much more common design because you can extend... You say, we need to add Facebook, need to add texting, you need to add Twitter, whatever. You can just extend this with all different choices.
cues.zh: 好，这是一种更常见的设计，因为你可以扩展……你说我们需要加Facebook、加短信、加Twitter之类的。你只需用各种不同的选项来扩展它。

cues.en: Alright. So,
cues.zh: 好，那么，

cues.en: to sum up, we've used code
cues.zh: 总结一下，我们用代码

cues.en: to represent the shared mental model.
cues.zh: 来表示共享的心智模型。

cues.en: We've shown how designs can evolve. This is really important. You don't just want to get it right first time. It's not a big sign up front. Designs will evolve. You need to be able to have some way of embracing the change without being scared
cues.zh: 我们展示了设计如何演进。这非常重要。你不是只想一次就做对。这不是前期大设计。设计会演进。你需要有某种方式来拥抱变化，而不害怕

cues.en: to make changes. And I think you can see in this approach, it's quite easy to make changes and still be confident
cues.zh: 做出改动。我想你能从这个方法中看到，做改动相当容易，而且仍然有信心

cues.en: that you, you know, that you have a good design. And this refactoring towards deeper insight is really...
cues.zh: 你知道，你有好的设计。而这种为了更深洞察而进行的重构，真的……

cues.en: So static typing, I think, very, good here. If you're trying to do this in Python or Ruby, something I really wouldn't be as confident about making all these...
cues.zh: 所以我觉得静态类型在这里非常好用。要是换成 Python 或 Ruby，我在做这一堆重构时可真没这么足的底气……

cues.en: So composable type systems are awesome.
cues.zh: 所以说，可组合的类型系统太棒了。

cues.en: You can see that we got choices rather than inheritance. We used options instead of null. We used wrappers over and over again, and wrapping things and more wrappings.
cues.zh: 大家能看到，我们用的是选择分支而非继承；用 Option 代替了 null；还反复使用包装，包了一层又一层。

cues.en: And then finally, this think in your head, always try to make illegal states unrepresentable
cues.zh: 最后，请把这句话牢记在心：永远尽量让非法状态无法被表示，

cues.en: if you can.
cues.zh: 只要你能做到。

cues.en: So if you like this talk,
cues.zh: 如果大家喜欢这场演讲，

cues.en: I have this talk on video, and I'm going to probably put this one up there at some point. I have more videos. I have a book. If anyone has the book and they want me to deface it, I'll be quite happy to do that.
cues.zh: 这个演讲有录像，今天这场我回头大概也会上传。我还有更多视频，也写了一本书。如果有人买了书想让我“涂鸦”（签名），我非常乐意效劳。

cues.en: And contact me on Twitter if you've got any questions.
cues.zh: 有什么问题也可以在 Twitter 上联系我。

cues.en: And if you like this one, stay for the next talk in this room, Roman's talk, which is like a deeper dive into the same kind of thing. Thank you very much.
cues.zh: 要是喜欢这个话题，推荐留在这个房间听下一场 Roman 的演讲，他会对同类内容做更深入的探讨。非常感谢大家！
